abstract: Marc Andreessen's manifesto argues technology — including AI — produces broad prosperity, and that resistance to deployment is itself the primary risk. Frames AI development as a moral imperative and rejects framings that focus on concentrated harms.
keyFindings: AI development is framed as morally good and politically urgent
Resistance to AI deployment (regulation, safety prioritization, slowdown advocacy) framed as the principal danger
Does not engage empirically with labor displacement evidence or distributional outcomes
Influential in venture-capital and accelerationist circles as a rallying document
qualifiers: Tier 4 — opinion/advocacy from a major AI investor with direct financial interest in deployment speed. Treat as a position to be cited, not an evidentiary source.
